correctness.rationale: Conditionally expand the square of ||v||²+a²+2<v,X>; the term linear in <v,X> has mean zero. The martingale and Rademacher sum both have second moment equal to the partial sum of squared lengths. The fourth-moment increments therefore differ by 4 E[a²||v||²−<v,X>²], which telescopes. For nonzero v and a, d²=2a²(1−c), giving the exact ratio 2(1+c) of the defect integrand to the weighted squared distance wherever the latter is positive. Orthogonal independent fair steps attain R/D=1/2 and positive angles approaching zero give the limit 1/4. Zero integrands imply radial alignment at every nonzero state; conditional centering gives fair signs on that event, and neither defect nor distance imposes a direction at zero. Zero-length steps contribute nothing. Inspected CHECK.py: quartic moments and transverse term are rational; the angular-distance tests use floats, and the examples are not a proof of the universal statement.
residual_risks: No claim for random lengths or mere upper bounds; stability is weighted by the preceding squared radius.
